purpose: Authored native-generation requests and whole-file input hashes for the fixed smoothed-vocoder evaluation. No private regression inputs or recordings.
generation_note: TTS is stochastic. Repeating requests does not reproduce identical audio or hashes. The long supplement reuses two generated sources from the full-flow study; it is not new project-corpus data.
long_selection: The existing Spanish 142.88-second recording and longest English 252.08-second recording. Fixed before any smoothed-vocoder held-out output labels. Sources reused across methods; not newly generated voices or independent additions to the project corpus.

items.text: The garden behind the museum had always been quiet, but its paths were difficult to follow after heavy rain. A group of volunteers decided to improve the signs and repair the shallow channels beside the flower beds. Before starting, they watched how water moved across the ground and marked the wettest places on a map. One path needed a small drain, while another only needed a thin layer of gravel. The work took three weekends. On the first Saturday, a delivery arrived at the wrong gate, so the volunteers carried the materials across the courtyard in small loads. On the second, they discovered an old stone step beneath the soil and asked the museum staff to record it before moving anything. By the final afternoon, visitors could walk from the entrance to the pond without stepping into deep puddles. The new signs explained which route was suitable for wheelchairs and where the ground might still be slippery. A teacher brought her class to compare their drawings with the finished garden. The children noticed that the simplest repair had made the biggest difference: a clear channel that allowed rainwater to flow away from the main path.

La bibliotecaria encontró una caja de cartas antiguas detrás de un armario. Antes de ordenarlas, fotografió cada sobre y anotó los nombres que todavía podían leerse. Un vecino reconoció la dirección de su abuelo, pero no estaba seguro de la fecha. Decidieron comparar las cartas con otros documentos. Al final prepararon una pequeña exposición que distinguía los datos confirmados de las preguntas pendientes.

Près du phare, une équipe a installé un banc pour observer les oiseaux sans déranger leurs nids. Les visiteurs doivent rester sur le sentier et garder les chiens en laisse. Une affiche explique pourquoi certaines zones sont fermées au printemps. Le gardien vérifie les barrières chaque matin, puis note ses observations dans un carnet. Il ne publie aucune conclusion avant d'avoir comparé plusieurs journées.

Im Gemeinschaftshaus wurde ein Regal für geliehene Werkzeuge aufgestellt. Jede Schublade bekam ein deutliches Schild und eine Liste der enthaltenen Teile. Wer etwas ausleiht, trägt seinen Namen und das Rückgabedatum in ein Heft ein. Am Freitag prüft eine Helferin, ob die Geräte sauber und vollständig sind. Beschädigte Kabel werden sofort zur Seite gelegt und vor der nächsten Benutzung repariert.

आज सुबह संग्रहालय के कर्मचारियों ने पुराने नक्शों की एक पेटी खोली। कागज बहुत नाजुक था, इसलिए उन्होंने हर पन्ने को धीरे से उठाया और उसकी तस्वीर ली। एक नक्शे पर नदी का रास्ता आज से अलग दिखाई दे रहा था। टीम ने तुरंत कोई निष्कर्ष नहीं निकाला। उन्होंने पहले दूसरी किताबों और स्थानीय अभिलेखों से तारीख की पुष्टि करने का निर्णय लिया।
駅前の小さな店で、古い写真を集める展示会が開かれました。参加者は写真を持ち寄り、撮影した場所や季節について話しました。しかし、正確な日付が分からないものもありました。係の人は推測と確認済みの情報を別々に記録しました。後日、図書館の新聞を調べて、町の橋が完成した年を確かめる予定です。

في صباح هادئ، فتحت أمينة المكتبة صندوقا قديما يحتوي على خرائط ورسائل. وضعت كل ورقة على طاولة نظيفة، ثم سجلت حالتها قبل تصويرها. لاحظ أحد الزوار أن اسم شارع تغير مع مرور الزمن، لكنه لم يتذكر السنة بدقة. لذلك لم تعتمد الفريق على الذاكرة وحدها. قرر الأعضاء مراجعة سجلات البلدية ومقارنة التواريخ قبل إعداد لوحة تشرح تاريخ الحي.
마을 회관에서는 오래된 사진을 모아 작은 전시회를 준비했습니다. 주민들은 사진 속 건물과 사람에 대해 아는 내용을 종이에 적었습니다. 날짜가 확실하지 않은 사진에는 별도의 표시를 붙였습니다. 담당자는 서로 다른 기억을 지우지 않고 모두 보관했습니다. 다음 주에는 도서관의 신문 자료를 찾아 사진이 찍힌 시기를 확인할 예정입니다.
社区图书馆收到了一箱旧照片。工作人员先给每张照片编号，再记录背面的文字。有位居民认出了河边的木桥，却不能确定照片拍摄的年份。大家没有急着写下结论，而是查阅当年的报纸和地图。他们希望在展览开放之前，把已经确认的事实和仍然存在的问题清楚地区分开。

В небольшом музее решили привести в порядок старые фотографии. Сотрудники записали все подписи и осторожно очистили рамки. Один посетитель узнал на снимке дом своего деда, но не смог назвать точный год. Поэтому рядом с фотографией оставили вопросительный знак. На следующей неделе команда сравнит снимок с городскими картами и газетами, прежде чем обновлять описание выставки.

இன்று காலை நூலக ஊழியர்கள் பழைய புகைப்படங்கள் இருந்த ஒரு பெட்டியைத் திறந்தனர். ஒவ்வொரு படத்திற்கும் தனி எண் கொடுத்து, அதன் பின்னால் இருந்த குறிப்புகளைப் பதிவு செய்தனர். ஒரு படத்தில் இருந்த பாலத்தை ஒருவர் அடையாளம் கண்டார். ஆனால் அது எப்போது எடுக்கப்பட்டது என்று அவருக்குத் தெரியவில்லை. எனவே பழைய செய்தித்தாள்களையும் வரைபடங்களையும் ஒப்பிட்ட பிறகே விளக்கத்தை எழுத முடிவு செய்தனர்.

وصل المتطوعون إلى الحديقة قبل الظهر، ومعهم أدوات صغيرة لتنظيف الممرات. طلب المشرف ألا يقطعوا أي غصن قبل التأكد من نوع الشجرة. وجدوا بطاقة قديمة قرب السياج، فاحتفظوا بها وسألوا البستاني عن معناها. بعد الاستراحة كتبوا قائمة بما أنجزوه وما يحتاج إلى مراجعة. لم يغيروا موعد الزيارة، بل أضافوا ملاحظة واضحة عن الطريق الذي ما زال مغلقا.

El pequeño museo del barrio ocupaba la planta baja de una antigua escuela. Durante años, sus salas habían reunido fotografías, herramientas y objetos donados por los vecinos. La colección era interesante, pero muchas piezas tenían etiquetas incompletas. Algunas fotografías mostraban calles que ya habían cambiado de nombre, y nadie estaba seguro de cuándo se habían tomado.

Un grupo de voluntarios decidió revisar el catálogo con ayuda de la biblioteca municipal. Antes de mover los objetos, prepararon una mesa de trabajo y asignaron un número a cada pieza. Después fotografiaron las etiquetas existentes, incluso las que parecían equivocadas. Conservar esa información permitiría entender cómo se había organizado la colección en otras épocas.

La primera semana apareció una caja de negativos detrás de un armario. Las imágenes mostraban un mercado al aire libre, una fábrica junto al río y varios grupos de estudiantes. Una vecina reconoció la fachada de la fábrica, pero recordó que el puente de la fotografía se había construido después de la fecha escrita en la caja. Los voluntarios anotaron la contradicción y buscaron planos antiguos para comprobarla.

No todas las preguntas tenían una respuesta rápida. Dos herramientas parecían iguales, aunque se habían utilizado para trabajos distintos. Un cuaderno mencionaba un taller que no figuraba en el directorio comercial de la época. En lugar de completar los espacios con suposiciones, el equipo dejó notas claras sobre lo que se sabía y lo que seguía pendiente. Esas dudas también formaban parte de la historia de los objetos.

Al terminar el mes, prepararon una exposición pequeña sobre el propio proceso de investigación. Junto a cada fotografía colocaron una copia de la información original y una explicación de las comprobaciones realizadas. Los visitantes podían ver por qué una fecha se había corregido o por qué otra seguía siendo aproximada. Una mesa al final de la sala ofrecía papel para añadir recuerdos, siempre con una forma de distinguir los testimonios de los documentos.

La exposición atrajo a personas que nunca habían entrado en el museo. Un antiguo conductor identificó una parada de autobús que aparecía al fondo de una imagen. Una profesora encontró el nombre de su primera escuela en un registro. Cada aportación se revisó con el mismo cuidado que las anteriores. El catálogo no quedó terminado para siempre, pero se convirtió en una herramienta más clara, abierta a nuevas preguntas y a futuras correcciones.

The old railway station stood between the river and a row of small shops. Passenger trains had stopped calling there many years earlier, but the building remained a familiar landmark. People still gave directions by referring to its clock tower, even though the clock no longer kept reliable time. When the town council invited ideas for a new use, the most popular suggestion was a public reading room with space for local history.

The volunteers began with a survey rather than a shopping list. They measured the rooms, photographed the damaged windows, and asked an engineer to inspect the roof. The largest room had excellent daylight but very few electrical sockets. A narrow room beside it was quiet enough for studying, while the former ticket office could become a place to borrow books. The group wrote down these observations so that later decisions would have clear reasons behind them.

Not everyone wanted the same arrangement. Parents asked for somewhere children could sit together without being told to whisper. Students wanted tables where they could spread out their notes. Older residents suggested comfortable chairs near the windows. Instead of treating these requests as a competition, the volunteers used a simple scale drawing to explore several layouts. Moving a paper table was much easier than moving a real one after the room had been painted.

The work took place over several weekends. One team cleaned the walls and repaired the shelves. Another sorted donated books into broad groups, setting aside damaged copies for a second look. A carpenter made a low display stand from timber left over from an earlier repair. Nothing about the project moved particularly quickly. A late delivery of paint delayed one room, and a leaking pipe briefly turned the kitchen floor into a shallow pond. Each problem went into the same notebook as the successful tasks.

As opening day approached, the volunteers tested the building as visitors would use it. They walked from the entrance to the reading tables, checked whether the signs were easy to understand, and tried the lights at different times of day. A student noticed that one shelf blocked the view of the children's corner. Someone else found that the return box was difficult to reach from a wheelchair. Both changes were small enough to make before the first visitors arrived.

On the opening morning, the reading room filled gradually. A delivery driver came in during a break to read the newspaper. Two children chose books about animals and compared the pictures on the carpet. Near the window, a retired railway worker explained an old photograph to a teenager who was researching the town's bridges. Their conversation became the first entry in a folder of local memories, with a note about which details still needed to be checked.

By the end of the month, the volunteers had learned more from ordinary use than from their original plans. The busiest table was not the largest one, and the quiet room was especially popular on rainy afternoons. They adjusted the opening hours, added a lamp beside a dark shelf, and kept a small supply of pencils at the desk. The station had not become a grand monument. It had become a useful place, shaped by the patient attention of the people who used it.

During the first winter, the building presented a new set of practical questions. Cold air entered around one window, and visitors tended to leave their coats on when they sat nearby. A volunteer measured the gap and found a simple repair that could be made without replacing the frame. Another person checked how the heating behaved when the main room was full. Their observations helped the group make small adjustments before considering expensive changes.

The local history folder also continued to grow. A shopkeeper brought a photograph of a parade that had passed the station decades earlier. Someone recognised a banner but disagreed about the year. The volunteers recorded both accounts and compared them with old newspaper pages. They found a report of heavy rain on the day of one possible parade, while the people in the photograph stood beneath a bright sky. That did not settle the question completely, but it gave them a useful reason to keep looking.

By spring, the reading room had become part of the town's ordinary routine. People came in to borrow a book, ask a question, or simply spend a quiet half hour beside a window. The volunteers kept their notebook at the desk, with separate pages for repairs, suggestions, and unanswered historical questions. It reminded them that caring for a place was an ongoing activity. A useful building did not need a perfect final plan. It needed people who were willing to notice what was happening and respond with patience.
